answer: An agent economy resists sybils by demanding a costly signal before any identity can trade: each agent locks a deposit and must first finish real, peer-verified jobs, like a traveller proving it crossed a desert to reach an oasis before it may drink the nectar of shared rewards. A fake identity can copy a name for free, but it cannot fake a long history of useful work plus a deposit it loses when caught cheating, so spawning a thousand fakes costs a thousand deposits and a thousand job histories.
